provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: The rule is direction-equivariant: for each cross, the centre is the cell whose four orthogonal neighbours share its colour. The pointer is the longest arm. The marker colour (palette[0]) goes on the grid edge in the pointer's direction, on the line through the centre. The cross's own colour goes on the opposite edge. Because the mechanism refers only to visible directions (up/down/left/right relative to the centre), it works directly in visible coordinates under every D4 transform without any rewriting of axes. Colour roles are specialised as constants: the marker is palette[0]. Crosses are processed in generator order, i.e. original colours 2, 5, 8, 9 mapped through the palette. So if two crosses' edge marks hit the same frame cell, the later write wins, matching the constructor's overwrite order rather than the archived solver's bounding-box order. Frame and background colours never need to be identified explicitly.
draft_notes.limitations: Assumes the constructor's domain: four distinct-colour crosses fully inside a frame, each with exactly one length-2 arm. If a cross were missing its centre it is skipped. Edge-collision resolution follows the generator's colour order (2, 5, 8, 9) through the palette. The archived solver instead uses spatial order, so the two could differ only in such rare collisions. No fixture contradiction was observed. The factory has not been tested.
